lesson.title: What makes an element?

steps.headline: An element is set by its number of protons, called the atomic number.

lead.text: An atom has a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it. The number of protons is the atomic number, written Z.
Change Z and you have a different element. Every sodium atom has 11 protons; an atom with 12 is magnesium.
Both atoms are drawn with their particle counts. Only one of those counts names the element.

reveal.text: You read the atomic number from the protons alone. Oxygen has 8 of them, and the neutron and electron counts happened to match.

steps.headline: Neutrons and electrons can change while the element stays the same.

lead.text: A neutron adds mass to the nucleus but no charge, so the element is unchanged. An electron changes the charge but leaves the nucleus alone.

steps.headline: How many electrons does a neutral lithium atom have? Its atomic number is 3.

workedSteps.text: Atomic number 3 means 3 protons. Each carries +1.
A neutral atom has no overall charge, so the electrons must cancel that.
Each electron carries −1, so it takes 3 of them.

steps.headline: A neutral nitrogen atom has 7 protons. How many electrons does it have?

workedSteps.text: Count the electrons that cancel it.

lead.text: Neutrons do not count towards charge or identity.
An ion is an atom that has gained or lost electrons. Aluminium has atomic number 13.

lesson.orientation: Use protons to identify an element and separate identity from mass and charge.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: Atom A has 6 protons, 6 neutrons and 6 electrons. Atom B has 6 protons, 7 neutrons and 6 electrons. Both are carbon. Atom C has 7 protons, 7 neutrons and 7 electrons. It is not carbon.

intro.promise: By the end you'll tell which element an atom is from its particle counts, and say what changes when neutrons or electrons do.

recap.keyIdea: An element is set by its proton count, the atomic number. Neutrons change an atom's mass and electrons change its charge, but neither changes the element.

blocks.text: You saw that two carbon atoms can differ in neutrons and still be carbon. You found that a neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, and that a nucleus holds only protons and neutrons.

recap.nextHook: Atoms of one element can still differ in mass. Next: how many neutrons, and what that does to mass.

questions.prompt: Oxygen has 8 protons, 8 neutrons and 8 electrons. What is its atomic number?
hints: Choose the particle that identifies the element.
Z counts protons; it ignores neutrons and electrons.
Which supplied count is the definition of atomic number?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Atomic number counts protons, so Z = 8.

questions.onCorrect: 8. The atomic number is the proton count, whatever the neutrons and electrons are doing.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the neutrons. The atomic number counts one kind of particle only.

questions.prompt: The two carbon cases differ in neutron count. Why are they both carbon?
hints: Compare the nuclei's proton counts.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Each nucleus still contains six protons.

questions.onCorrect: Same proton count, same element. The extra neutron changes the mass, not the identity.

misconceptions.feedback: The masses differ here: one has an extra neutron. Look for the count that stays fixed.
The totals differ, because one nucleus has an extra neutron. Look for what stays fixed.

questions.prompt: A neutral nitrogen atom has 7 protons. How many electrons does it have?
hints: Neutral means no net electric charge.
Each proton is +1 and each electron is −1.
How many negative charges cancel the nucleus's positive charge?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Seven electrons cancel the charge of seven protons.

questions.onCorrect: 7. Seven electrons cancel the charge of seven protons, so a neutral atom has equal counts.

misconceptions.feedback: Neutral means the charges cancel, not that there are no electrons.
That adds the neutrons. Neutrons carry no charge, so they play no part in cancelling.

questions.prompt: Aluminium has atomic number 13. How many protons does an aluminium ion contain?
hints: An ion retains its element's nucleus.
Ion formation changes electrons, not the atomic number.
Read the stated atomic number without adjusting it for ion charge.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Ion formation changes electrons, so its thirteen protons remain.

questions.onCorrect: 13. Forming an ion changes the electrons only, so the proton count stays the atomic number.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the electron count of the ion. The nucleus keeps its own protons.
Check what the question gives you: the atomic number is the proton count.
That is the atom's mass number. Protons are counted alone.

questions.prompt: Which change makes a carbon atom an atom of a different element?
hints: Distinguish identity from charge and mass.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Changing the proton count changes the atomic number.

questions.onCorrect: Adding a proton changes the atomic number, so it makes a different element.

misconceptions.feedback: A neutron changes the mass, not the element: the proton count is the same.
Losing an electron makes an ion of carbon. The nucleus, and the element, are the same.

questions.prompt: A fluorine nucleus contains 9 protons and 10 neutrons. How many particles are in its nucleus?
hints: Which particles are inside the nucleus?
Leave the electrons out of the count.
Add the protons to the neutrons.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Only protons and neutrons are in the nucleus: 9 + 10 = 19.

questions.onCorrect: 19. The nucleus holds protons and neutrons only. Electrons are outside it.

misconceptions.feedback: That counts the protons alone. The neutrons are in the nucleus too.
That counts the neutrons alone. The protons are in the nucleus too.

questions.prompt: Which number is the same in both carbon atoms, A and B?
hints: Put A and B side by side. Which counts match?
A and B have different neutron counts, so that cannot be the shared number.
Look at the counts that match, and check that C's differs.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Both have 6 protons and 6 electrons. Atom C has 7, so the shared number is 6.

questions.onCorrect: 6. Neutrons can differ and the atom is still carbon. The count that matches is the proton count.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the neutron count of B. A has a different one, and both are carbon.
Those are totals. A and B have different totals, yet both are carbon.

questions.prompt: An atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. What is its atomic number?
hints: Which particle count is the atomic number?
Neutrons are not counted.
Read the proton count straight off the question.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Atomic number is the proton count: 6.

questions.onCorrect: 6. The atomic number is the proton count and nothing else.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the neutron count. The atomic number is the number of protons.
That adds the neutrons to the protons. The atomic number is protons alone.

questions.prompt: Why must a neutral atom have as many electrons as protons?

acceptedIdeas: Each electron's negative charge cancels one proton's positive charge
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Equal numbers of +1 and −1 charges cancel exactly.

choices.label: Each electron's negative charge cancels one proton's positive charge
Electrons and protons have the same mass
The neutrons carry the leftover charge

questions.onCorrect: Right: equal numbers of positive and negative charges leave no net charge.

misconceptions.feedback: Mass does not matter here. This is about electric charge.
Neutrons carry no charge, so they cannot hold any leftover.

questions.prompt: A neutral atom has 9 electrons and 10 neutrons. What is its atomic number?
hints: What does neutral tell you about electrons and protons?
The atomic number is the proton count.
Ignore the neutrons and match the electrons.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Neutral means 9 protons to match 9 electrons, so Z = 9.

questions.onCorrect: 9. Neutral means protons equal electrons, and the atomic number is the proton count.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the neutron count. It has no effect on the atomic number.
That adds the neutrons. The atomic number is protons alone.

questions.prompt: A neutral atom has 14 electrons and 16 neutrons. How many particles are in its nucleus?
hints: How many protons does a neutral atom with 14 electrons have?
The nucleus holds protons and neutrons.
Add the protons to the neutrons.
questions.onCorrect: 30. Neutral gives 14 protons, and the nucleus holds protons plus neutrons.

misconceptions.feedback: That counts neutrons only. The protons are in the nucleus too.
That includes the electrons, which are outside the nucleus.
That counts protons only. The neutrons are in the nucleus too.
